docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Welcome to the Appium WinCore driver documentation! The WinCore driver automates Windows desktop applications (UWP, WinForms, WPF, Win32, WebView2 and Internet Explorer) through real UI Automation.

The WinCore driver is part of the Appium test automation tool. For information on Appium itself, please visit the Appium documentation.

Developed and supported by

docs.title: Explore the Documentation
docs.text:
• Check out the Overview to learn how the driver works
  • Go through the Getting Started steps to get set up
  • Browse the Reference documentation for everything exposed by the driver
  • Read the different Guides for a variety of instructions, tips and tricks
  • For contributions to the driver, refer to the Contributing page

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The WinCore driver is an Appium driver intended for black-box automated testing of Windows desktop applications through the standard WebDriver API.

docs.title: Target Platforms
docs.text:
The driver supports the following Windows platforms as automation targets:

Platform Supported Windows 10 Windows 11 Windows Server 1 Windows IoT 2

docs.title: Target Applications
docs.text:
The driver can automate any application whose user interface is exposed through Microsoft UI Automation (UIA):

Application type What the driver reaches UWP, Win32, WinForms, WPF Every UIA-visible control, including raw-view elements hidden from the control view WebView2, Chrome, Edge Embedded web content over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, from the same session. See the Hybrid Mode guide Internet Explorer 11 HTML content through the built-in IE DOM bridge. See the Internet Explorer guide Legacy MSAA grids and controls Content hidden behind placeholder names, through standard accessibility values

The following application types are not supported out of the box:

  • Java applications (Swing, AWT, and other JVM UI toolkits). Their controls are not exposed to UIA, so the driver only sees the top-level window.
  • Any other application that does not expose its user interface through UIA or MSAA, for example applications that draw all of their controls themselves.
  • Internet Explorer versions older than 11.

Support for such applications can be added with server plugins, which provide element trees from outside of UIA.

docs.title: Technologies Used
docs.text:
The WinCore driver uses the W3C WebDriver protocol for session management. Under the hood, the driver combines several different technologies to achieve its functionality:

  • Native testing
    • Based on Microsoft UI Automation (UIA3), the accessibility framework that exposes the user interface of Windows applications
    • Provided by WincoreServer.exe, a .NET process bundled with the driver that lives for the length of the session. It handles element finding, UIA patterns, XPath, page source, process and window management, the clipboard, screenshots, file operations and PowerShell execution
    • Legacy controls with no UIA children fall back to the Microsoft Active Accessibility (MSAA) tree
  • Input
    • Mouse and keyboard input is sent directly through the Windows SendInput API, called from Node.js through the koffi library
  • Webview testing
    • Based on the ChromeDriver server and Microsoft Edge WebDriver
    • Provided by the appium-chromedriver library
  • Internet Explorer testing
    • Provided by IEBridge.exe, a 32-bit process bundled with the driver that reads the IE DOM through COM
  • Additional tools
    • Screen recording is handled by FFmpeg
    • Element trees outside of UIA can be provided by server plugins

docs.title: Server Plugins
docs.text: To extend the driver with element trees from outside of UI Automation, see Server Plugins.

docs.title: Server Plugins
docs.text:
This page is intended for developers who want to extend the driver. A server plugin can provide elements for applications whose user interface is not exposed through UI Automation.

WincoreServer.exe loads external .NET plugins at startup. A plugin adds JSON-RPC command handlers and one tree provider: a source of elements that live outside the real UIA tree.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
The server reads plugin directories from the WINCORE_SERVER_PLUGINS environment variable (;-separated). Typically an Appium plugin sets it before the driver spawns the server.

Each plugin directory contains:

  • plugin.json — the manifest
  • an assembly implementing IServerPlugin

The contract is published as the WincoreServerSdk NuGet package (source: csharp/WincoreServerSdk/). The loader and registry live in csharp/WincoreServer/Plugins/.

docs.title: Tree providers
docs.text:
An ITreeProvider owns elements addressed by an element-id prefix (for example myprovider:).

Element-scoped commands are routed centrally. Each command is registered in CommandDispatcher.AddElementRoutes with:

  • a UIA handler, which receives the resolved UIA element, and
  • a provider handler (ElementRoute), which receives the provider element.

Handlers never inspect ids themselves. A command with no provider handler is UIA-only — window operations and the session root, for example.

Find, XPath and page source are routed per window (TryResolveWindow(hwnd)) and stay bespoke in their handlers.

FindItemInContainer is optional. It backs windows: selectFromCombobox, and can return entries a container has not created yet. When a provider does not implement it, or returns null, the driver searches the container's current descendants instead.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: New ITreeProvider capabilities get a default "not supported" implementation, so plugins built against an older SDK keep loading.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
There are three primary requirements to use the WinCore driver:

  • Windows host machine (see Target Platforms)
  • Node.js ^22.22.2, ^24.15.0 or >=26.0.0
  • Appium

The application under test must run on the same machine as the Appium server, in an interactive desktop session: UI Automation and input synthesis need a live, unlocked desktop.

docs.title: Appium Server
docs.text:
Make sure to install a version of Appium that supports your target driver version. The requirements and prerequisites of Appium itself can be found in the Appium documentation.

WinCore driver version Supported Appium server version >= 4.0.0 Appium 4 < 4.0.0 Appium 3

Note

Appium 4 is currently published under the npm beta tag, so it must be requested explicitly. A plain npm install -g appium installs Appium 3, which the latest driver version does not support:

npm install -g appium@beta

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Provided you have set up the above prerequisites, you can install the driver using Appium's extension CLI:

appium driver install --source=npm appium-wincore-driver

You can also specify an exact driver version:

appium driver install --source=npm appium-wincore-driver@4.0.9

Alternatively, if you are running a Node.js project, you can include appium-wincore-driver as one of your project dependencies. Refer to the Appium documentation for more information about this approach.

docs.title: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
In order to check that the driver was installed correctly, simply launch the Appium server:

appium

The server log output should include a line like the following:

[Appium] AppiumWincoreDriver has been successfully loaded in 0.780s

By default the server listens on http://127.0.0.1:4723.

docs.title: Creating a Session
docs.text:
The WinCore driver, like all Appium drivers, requires providing specific capabilities in order to start a new session. The following example lists the minimum required capabilities for a basic session:

// This will start a session that launches Windows Calculator
{
  "platformName": "Windows",
  "appium:automationName": "Wincore",
  "appium:app": "Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App"
}

appium:app accepts an .exe path, a UWP application user model ID (as above), or Root to attach to the whole desktop. To attach to a window that is already open instead, use appium:appTopLevelWindow.

See the Capabilities reference page for more information on the capabilities supported by the driver, and the Examples guide for complete tests in several client languages.

docs.title: W3C Actions
docs.text: The driver implements the W3C WebDriver Actions API. Supported input source types: pointer (mouse only; touch/pen not supported), key, wheel, and none.

docs.title: Tick ordering
docs.text:
Actions are processed tick by tick. All actions at the same tick index across input sources run simultaneously (Promise.all). Ticks advance sequentially. Use pause entries to align sources.

// Tick 1: keyDown and pointerDown fire at the same time
await driver.performActions([
  {
    type: 'key',
    id: 'keyboard',
    actions: [
      { type: 'pause' },                     // tick 0
      { type: 'keyDown', value: '\uE009' },  // tick 1 — simultaneous
      { type: 'keyUp', value: '\uE009' },    // tick 2
    ],
  },
  {
    type: 'pointer',
    id: 'mouse',
    parameters: { pointerType: 'mouse' },
    actions: [
      { type: 'pointerMove', duration: 0, x: 100, y: 200 }, // tick 0
      { type: 'pointerDown', button: 0 },                    // tick 1
      { type: 'pointerUp', button: 0 },                      // tick 2
    ],
  },
]);
await driver.releaseActions();

Always call driver.releaseActions() after performActions() to release any held keys or mouse buttons.

docs.title: Windows Calculator: your first test
docs.text:
This test opens Windows Calculator, computes 5 + 3 and reads the result. It assumes an Appium server with the driver installed is running on http://127.0.0.1:4723 (see Getting Started).

JavaScript (WebdriverIO)PythonC# 
npm install webdriverio

import { remote } from 'webdriverio';

const driver = await remote({
  hostname: '127.0.0.1',
  port: 4723,
  capabilities: {
    platformName: 'Windows',
    'appium:automationName': 'Wincore',
    'appium:app': 'Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App',
  },
});

for (const id of ['num5Button', 'plusButton', 'num3Button', 'equalButton']) {
  await driver.$(`~${id}`).click();
}

console.log(await driver.$('~CalculatorResults').getText());
await driver.deleteSession();

pip install Appium-Python-Client

from appium import webdriver
from appium.options.common import AppiumOptions
from appium.webdriver.common.appiumby import AppiumBy

options = AppiumOptions()
options.load_capabilities({
    "platformName": "Windows",
    "appium:automationName": "Wincore",
    "appium:app": "Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App",
})
driver = webdriver.Remote("http://127.0.0.1:4723", options=options)

for key in ("num5Button", "plusButton", "num3Button", "equalButton"):
    driver.find_element(AppiumBy.ACCESSIBILITY_ID, key).click()

print(driver.find_element(AppiumBy.ACCESSIBILITY_ID, "CalculatorResults").text)
driver.quit()

dotnet add package Appium.WebDriver

using OpenQA.Selenium.Appium;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Appium.Windows;

var options = new AppiumOptions
{
    PlatformName = "Windows",
    AutomationName = "Wincore",
    App = "Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App",
};
using var driver = new WindowsDriver(new Uri("http://127.0.0.1:4723/"), options);

foreach (var id in new[] { "num5Button", "plusButton", "num3Button", "equalButton" })
    driver.FindElement(MobileBy.AccessibilityId(id)).Click();

Console.WriteLine(driver.FindElement(MobileBy.AccessibilityId("CalculatorResults")).Text);

From here, you can explore the element tree with Appium Inspector or driver.getPageSource(), learn the locator strategies, or browse the windows: execute methods.

docs.title: Desktop root: click an icon and switch windows
docs.text:
import { remote } from 'webdriverio';

const driver = await remote({
  hostname: '127.0.0.1',
  port: 4723,
  path: '/',
  capabilities: {
    platformName: 'Windows',
    'appium:automationName': 'Wincore',
    'appium:app': 'Root', // attach to the Windows desktop shell
  },
});

// Double-click a desktop shortcut by its accessible name
const icon = await driver.$('~Notepad');
await driver.executeScript('windows: click', [{
  elementId: icon.elementId,
  times: 2,
  interClickDelayMs: 100,
}]);

// Give the app time to open, then switch to the new window by handle...
await driver.pause(2000);
const allHandles = await driver.getWindowHandles();
await driver.switchToWindow(allHandles[allHandles.length - 1]);

// ...or switch by title (partial, case-insensitive)
await driver.executeScript('windows: switchToWindowByTitle', [{ title: 'Notepad' }]);

// To include untitled windows (getWindowHandles omits them), use getWindows instead.
// It returns { handle, title, className } for every visible top-level window.
const windows = await driver.executeScript('windows: getWindows', []);
const popup = windows.find(w => w.className === '#32770' && w.title === '');
if (popup) await driver.switchToWindow(popup.handle);

const titleBar = await driver.$('//TitleBar');
console.log(await titleBar.getText());

// Switch back to the desktop root at any time
await driver.switchToWindow('root');

await driver.deleteSession();

docs.title: Windows Calculator: invoke pattern
docs.text:
windows: invoke fires the UIA InvokePattern. Prefer it over .click() for controls that do not respond reliably to pointer events.

import { remote } from 'webdriverio';

const driver = await remote({
  hostname: '127.0.0.1',
  port: 4723,
  path: '/',
  capabilities: {
    platformName: 'Windows',
    'appium:automationName': 'Wincore',
    'appium:app': 'Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App',
  },
});

async function invoke(el) {
  await driver.executeScript('windows: invoke', [el]);
}

// 5 + 3 =
await invoke(await driver.$('~num5Button'));
await invoke(await driver.$('~plusButton'));
await invoke(await driver.$('~num3Button'));
await invoke(await driver.$('~equalButton'));

const display = await driver.$('~CalculatorResults');
console.log(await display.getText()); // "Display is 8"

await driver.deleteSession();

docs.title: Ctrl+drag via W3C Actions
docs.text:
Actions are processed tick by tick. All actions at the same tick index across input sources run simultaneously. Ticks advance sequentially. Use pause entries to keep sources aligned when mixing keyboard and pointer inputs.

import { remote } from 'webdriverio';

const driver = await remote({
  hostname: '127.0.0.1',
  port: 4723,
  path: '/',
  capabilities: {
    platformName: 'Windows',
    'appium:automationName': 'Wincore',
    'appium:app': 'C:\\MyApp\\app.exe',
  },
});

const source = await driver.$('~dragSource');
const target = await driver.$('~dropTarget');

await driver.performActions([
  {
    type: 'key',
    id: 'keyboard',
    actions: [
      { type: 'pause' },                    // tick 0 — wait for mouse move
      { type: 'keyDown', value: '\uE009' }, // tick 1 — Ctrl key (W3C key value)
      { type: 'pause' },                    // tick 2 — hold
      { type: 'pause' },                    // tick 3 — hold during drag
      { type: 'keyUp', value: '\uE009' },   // tick 4 — Ctrl up
    ],
  },
  {
    type: 'pointer',
    id: 'mouse',
    parameters: { pointerType: 'mouse' },
    actions: [
      { type: 'pointerMove', duration: 0, origin: source },   // tick 0
      { type: 'pointerDown', button: 0 },                      // tick 1
      { type: 'pause', duration: 300 },                        // tick 2
      { type: 'pointerMove', duration: 600, origin: target },  // tick 3
      { type: 'pointerUp', button: 0 },                        // tick 4
    ],
  },
]);

await driver.releaseActions();
await driver.deleteSession();

docs.title: Hybrid Mode
docs.text:
The WinCore driver supports automation of hybrid apps that use Chromium-based web views, such as WebView2 or Electron apps, as well as the Chrome and Edge browsers. This enables actions such as retrieving the web-specific page source, as well as finding and interacting with elements located inside the web view.

Warning

Web content based on other engines is not supported through this mode. Internet Explorer 11 is supported through a separate bridge, described in the Internet Explorer guide. Other web views are only available through the native UI Automation tree.

docs.title: Enabling Hybrid Mode
docs.text:
Access to web views is not available by default, and must be explicitly enabled by setting the appium:webviewEnabled capability to true.

The driver connects to the web view through its Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) remote debugging port. How this port is set depends on the application:

  • WebView2 apps launched by the driver: no additional configuration is needed. The driver selects a free port and passes it to the app through the WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS environment variable.

    {
  "platformName": "Windows",
  "appium:automationName": "Wincore",
  "appium:app": "C:\\Path\\To\\YourApp.exe",
  "appium:webviewEnabled": true
}

  • Chrome or Edge launched by the driver: the browser must be started with a debugging port and a dedicated profile, using appium:appArguments, and the same port must be provided in appium:webviewDevtoolsPort. The dedicated profile (--user-data-dir) isolates the session from any running browser instance.

    {
  "platformName": "Windows",
  "appium:automationName": "Wincore",
  "appium:app": "C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe",
  "appium:appArguments": "--remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=C:\\Temp\\cr-test",
  "appium:webviewEnabled": true,
  "appium:webviewDevtoolsPort": 9222
}

  • Apps that are already running, attached with appium:appTopLevelWindow or reached from a Root session: the app must already expose a debugging port, and that port must be provided in appium:webviewDevtoolsPort.

The availability of a particular web view can be verified with the Chrome Remote Debugger, or by opening http://localhost:<port>/json/list in a browser.

docs.title: Contexts
docs.text:
Web-specific information is not directly integrated into the default page source. Instead, the driver makes use of Appium's Context Management API, where each available web page is separated into its own context. As such, in order to interact with any web view, it is necessary to first switch to its specific context using the context API.

A WinCore driver session starts in the native context (named NATIVE_APP). Each page exposed by the web view's debugging port is available as an additional WEBVIEW_<id> context. To retrieve detailed information about these pages, the driver also provides the mobile: getContexts execute method, which accepts an optional waitForWebviewMs argument to wait for the web view to load:

const contexts = await driver.executeScript('mobile: getContexts', [{waitForWebviewMs: 2000}]);
// [
//   { id: 'NATIVE_APP' },
//   { id: 'WEBVIEW_...', title: 'My Page', url: '...', type: 'page' }
// ]

const webId = contexts.find((c) => c.id.startsWith('WEBVIEW_')).id;

// Switch to the web context
await driver.switchContext(webId);
const title = await driver.getTitle();

// Back to the native context
await driver.switchContext('NATIVE_APP');

In practice, when switching the application context from native to web view, the WinCore driver simply changes the underlying component to which it forwards most API commands:

  • Native context: WincoreServer.exe (UI Automation)
  • Web view context: an instance of ChromeDriver or Microsoft Edge WebDriver

Refer to Technologies Used for more details.

docs.title: Web Context Specifics
docs.text:
Switching from the native context to a web context brings a few benefits and drawbacks alike:

  • Web view-specific page source with web elements, similar to the one in Chrome DevTools
  • Support for standard W3C WebDriver element locator strategies
  • No support for driver-specific native locator strategies
  • The windows: execute methods are still handled by the native layer, while any other script is executed in the web page

Switching to the NATIVE_APP context stops the current ChromeDriver or Edge WebDriver instance.

docs.title: Managing ChromeDriver and Edge WebDriver
docs.text:
The driver reads the browser name and version from the web view, and uses ChromeDriver for Chrome and Electron, or Microsoft Edge WebDriver for Edge and WebView2. The version of this driver must follow the version of the browser engine used by the web view under test.

There are several approaches to obtaining a matching driver version:

docs.title: Automatic Download
docs.text: By default, the driver automatically downloads the version of ChromeDriver or Edge WebDriver that matches the web view under test. The download is initiated upon switching to the web view context, and requires internet access from the Appium server host. Downloaded executables are reused by later sessions.

docs.title: Using Capabilities
docs.text:
If the target driver executable already exists on the host machine, it is possible to provide a path to it using the appium:chromedriverExecutablePath or appium:edgedriverExecutablePath capability. In this case, nothing is downloaded, and the executable must match the version of the web view.

In order to manually download the correct executable, refer to the ChromeDriver Version Selection guide, or to the Microsoft Edge WebDriver download page.

docs.title: Downloading
docs.text:
In case of issues when downloading the driver executables, the download location can be changed with the appium:chromedriverCdnUrl and appium:edgedriverCdnUrl capabilities.

It may also be necessary to adjust network proxy and firewall settings for the above to work.

docs.title: Internet Explorer
docs.text: iexplore.exe exposes content via MSAA/COM, not UIA. The driver includes a built-in IE DOM Bridge — a 32-bit C# process (IEBridge.exe) that attaches to a running IE 11 window via the WM_HTML_GETOBJECT message, retrieves IHTMLDocument2 through COM, and routes element commands over stdio JSON. No WebDriver protocol proxy and no special capability is needed.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. A standard desktop session starts with UIA active.
  2. When switchToWindow or windows: switchToWindowByTitle targets an IEFrame window, the driver detects it automatically and spawns IEBridge.exe for that window handle.
  3. Element commands (findElement, click, getText, setValue, executeScript, switchToFrame, ...) are sent to the bridge process as JSON over stdin/stdout and resolved against the live IHTMLDocument2.
  4. Switching to a non-IE window tears down the IE session; UIA resumes.
  5. On deleteSession, the bridge process is killed and all state reset.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: No capability is required to automate IE.

docs.title: IE configuration (required)
docs.text:
Before automating IE, apply these settings in Internet Options:

  • Security tab — uncheck "Enable Protected Mode" on every zone (Internet, Local Intranet, Trusted Sites, Restricted Sites)
  • Advanced tab — uncheck "Enable Enhanced Protected Mode"
  • View menu — set Zoom to exactly 100%

docs.title: Mixed-window sessions
docs.text:
IE and non-IE windows can be used in the same session:

// Start a plain desktop session
const driver = await remote({ capabilities: { platformName: 'Windows',
  'appium:automationName': 'Wincore', 'appium:app': 'Root' } });

// Switch to IE — IE Bridge activates automatically
await driver.executeScript('windows: switchToWindowByTitle', [{ title: 'Internet Explorer' }]);
const h1 = await driver.$('h1');
console.log(await h1.getText()); // IE DOM result

// Switch to Notepad — UIA resumes automatically
await driver.executeScript('windows: switchToWindowByTitle', [{ title: 'Notepad' }]);
const src = await driver.getPageSource(); // UIA tree

// Switch back to IE — bridge re-activates
await driver.executeScript('windows: switchToWindowByTitle', [{ title: 'Internet Explorer' }]);

docs.title: Switching into frames
docs.text:
await driver.switchToFrame(0);           // by 0-based index
await driver.switchToFrame(frameEl);     // by element (find first)
await driver.switchToFrame(null);        // back to default content
await driver.switchToParentFrame();      // also returns to default content

Only one level of nesting is tracked — switchToParentFrame() always returns to the top-level document rather than popping a frame stack.

docs.title: Command support
docs.text: Command Status Notes findElement / findElements ✅ css selector, id, xpath getTitle ✅ getUrl ✅ getPageSource ✅ url() ✅ navigate to URL getWindowHandle ✅ returns HWND hex string getText(el) ✅ getAttribute(el, name) ✅ clear(el) ✅ input / textarea only setValue(el, value) ✅ input / textarea only click(el) ✅ / ⚠️ works for buttons, links; broken for checkboxes and radios isDisplayed(el) ✅ isEnabled(el) ⚠️ unreliable for elements without an id attribute isSelected(el) ❌ always returns false executeScript(script, args) ✅ runs JS in the IE tab switchToFrame(id) ✅ by index, element, or null for default content switchToParentFrame() ✅ returns to default content (single-level only) getElementRect(el) ❌ not implemented getElementScreenshot(el) ❌ not implemented windows: execute methods ❌ target the UIA tree, not the HTML DOM

docs.title: Locator strategies in IE windows
docs.text:
When the active window is IE, commands route through IEBridge. UIA-specific locators are not available — use:

css selector, id, xpath

Supported XPath patterns: //tag, //tag[@attr="val"], //tag[contains(text(),"...")], //tag[contains(@attr,"...")], //tag[@attr]

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
When the active window is IE, the following are not available: WebView2/CDP, screen recording, clipboard API, appium:prerun/appium:postrun, and UIA locator strategies (accessibility id, -windows uiautomation, class name).

windows: execute methods target the UIA tree and are not available while an IE window is active; use standard WebDriver equivalents (element.click(), driver.url(), executeScript) instead.

Supported on Windows 10/11 with IE 11 only.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text:
IE mode activates automatically whenever a session window has the IEFrame window class. This happens when:

  • appium:app is set to the IE executable and the driver launches it, or
  • appium:appTopLevelWindow points to an existing IE window handle, or
  • windows: switchToWindow / windows: switchToWindowByTitle targets an IE window.

docs.title: Launch IE and automate it
docs.text:
import { remote } from 'webdriverio';

const driver = await remote({
  hostname: '127.0.0.1',
  port: 4723,
  path: '/',
  capabilities: {
    platformName: 'Windows',
    'appium:automationName': 'Wincore',
    'appium:app': 'C:\\Program Files\\Internet Explorer\\iexplore.exe',
    'appium:appArguments': 'https://example.com',
    'appium:shouldCloseApp': true,
  },
});

await driver.pause(3000); // wait for IE to load the page
await driver.setTimeout({ implicit: 5000 });

const title = await driver.getTitle();
console.log(title); // "Example Domain"

const h1 = await driver.$('h1');
console.log(await h1.getText());

await driver.deleteSession();

docs.title: Attach to an already-open IE window
docs.text:
import { remote } from 'webdriverio';

// hwnd is the decimal or hex HWND string of the IEFrame window
const driver = await remote({
  hostname: '127.0.0.1',
  port: 4723,
  path: '/',
  capabilities: {
    platformName: 'Windows',
    'appium:automationName': 'Wincore',
    'appium:appTopLevelWindow': '0x001A0B2C',
    'appium:shouldCloseApp': false,
  },
});

const url = await driver.getUrl();
console.log(url);

await driver.deleteSession();

docs.title: Switch into an iframe
docs.text:
// By 0-based index
await driver.switchToFrame(0);

// By element
const frameEl = await driver.$('iframe#content');
await driver.switchToFrame(frameEl);

// Element finds are now scoped to the frame's document
const h1 = await driver.$('h1');
console.log(await h1.getText());

// Back to the top-level document
await driver.switchToFrame(null);

Only one level of nesting is tracked — switching into a frame while already inside one replaces the current frame context rather than stacking. switchToParentFrame() always returns to default content.

docs.title: Switch between IE and UIA within the same session
docs.text:
Start a Root session and navigate between windows freely. The driver switches between IE Bridge mode and UIA mode automatically based on whether the target window is an IEFrame.

import { remote } from 'webdriverio';

const driver = await remote({
  hostname: '127.0.0.1',
  port: 4723,
  path: '/',
  capabilities: {
    platformName: 'Windows',
    'appium:automationName': 'Wincore',
    'appium:app': 'Root',
  },
});

// Focus the IE window — IE Bridge activates automatically
await driver.executeScript('windows: switchToWindowByTitle', [{ title: 'Internet Explorer' }]);

const h1 = await driver.$('h1');
console.log(await h1.getText());

// Switch to a non-IE window — UIA resumes automatically
await driver.executeScript('windows: switchToWindowByTitle', [{ title: 'Notepad' }]);

await driver.deleteSession();

docs.title: Performance Metrics
docs.text: The WinCore driver can measure the time spent in some of its internal calls, which helps to understand why a command is slow. For example, it can show how much of a page source request or an XPath lookup was spent reading elements from the UI Automation tree.

docs.title: Enabling the Metrics
docs.text:
Metrics are collected per session, and only when the session is created with the appium:perfMetrics capability:

{
  "platformName": "Windows",
  "appium:automationName": "Wincore",
  "appium:app": "Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App",
  "appium:perfMetrics": true
}

Collecting the metrics adds almost no overhead.

docs.title: Reading and Resetting the Metrics
docs.text:
Two execute methods give access to the counters:

  • windows: getPerfMetrics returns the counters collected so far
  • windows: resetPerfMetrics sets them back to zero, so that the next reading only covers the operations that follow
await driver.executeScript('windows: resetPerfMetrics', []);
await driver.getPageSource();
const { enabled, metrics } = await driver.executeScript('windows: getPerfMetrics', []);

The result has the following shape:

{
  "enabled": true,
  "metrics": {
    "totalCalls": 3036,
    "totalMs": 4612.4,
    "byLabel": {
      "uia.pageSource.node": { "count": 3036, "totalMs": 4612.4 }
    }
  }
}

If the session was created without appium:perfMetrics, enabled is false and metrics is empty.

docs.title: Counter Labels
docs.text:
Label count totalMs uia.pageSource.node Elements read for the page source Time spent reading them uia.xpathModel.node Elements read for an XPath lookup Time spent reading them

Each element read costs about 1.5 ms on WPF applications, and more on WinForms and MSAA-based controls. If these counters dominate a slow test, see Absolute vs. Relative Lookup for ways to read fewer elements.

docs.title: Standard Accessibility Values
docs.text:
Many controls publish their real content through standard accessibility, but not in the UI Automation Name property. This is common for DevExpress grids and trees, the .NET Framework DataGridView, and other MSAA-based controls (VB6, Delphi, older MFC, third-party grids). For example, a grid cell's Name can be a placeholder such as Status row 2, while its content (Degraded) is in the MSAA value.

To reach such content, every element in the page source and in XPath carries the following attributes, with no plugin or capability needed:

Attribute Source Value ValuePattern.Value LegacyValue LegacyIAccessible.Value (MSAA accValue) LegacyName LegacyIAccessible.Name LegacyDescription LegacyIAccessible.Description LegacyRole LegacyIAccessible.Role (MSAA role number) LegacyState LegacyIAccessible.State (MSAA state bits)

docs.title: Finding Elements by Value
docs.text:
await driver.$('//DataItem[@LegacyValue="Degraded"]')
await driver.$('//*[starts-with(@LegacyValue, "db-01;")]')   // a whole grid row

Value and LegacyValue are usually equal on MSAA controls. Some elements, such as grid rows, only have LegacyValue. An attribute is empty when the element doesn't support it.

On large windows, find the grid first and search inside it, as described in Absolute vs. Relative Lookup.

docs.title: WPF and UWP Elements
docs.text: In the page source and XPath, the Legacy* attributes are empty on WPF and UWP (XAML) elements. Those frameworks have their own UIA provider, so there is no MSAA object behind them: UIA would build the legacy values from Name and Value at a high cost for every element. The Get Element Attribute endpoint still returns them for any single element.

docs.title: Passwords and Long Values
docs.text:
In the page source and XPath, Value and LegacyValue are always empty on password elements (IsPassword), even when the control itself would return its secret. If IsPassword can't be read, the element is treated as a password. Values are also cut to 4096 characters there, without splitting an emoji or other surrogate pair.

Warning

The Get Element Attribute endpoint reads a single element and is not filtered. getAttribute('Value') and getAttribute('LegacyValue') return the full value, and on a password element that can be the secret itself (as windows: getValue already does). Don't log those results.

Page source text keeps every character that XML allows, including emoji. Only characters that XML 1.0 cannot carry (control characters, unpaired surrogates) are removed.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
This page lists various capabilities used and implemented by the WinCore driver. To learn more about capabilities, refer to the Appium documentation.

For other capabilities recognized by the Appium server, see their Appium docs reference page.

docs.title: Standard
docs.text: Refer to the W3C WebDriver documentation for more information about these capabilities.

docs.title: platformName
docs.text:
Name Type Default platformName string Not specified

Must be set to Windows (case-insensitive).

docs.title: automationName
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:automationName string Not specified

Specifies the Appium driver to use. Must be set to Wincore (case-insensitive).

docs.title: logFile
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:logFile string or boolean Not specified

Mirrors the driver's session log to a file, in addition to the Appium server log. Accepts:

  • true: writes to a timestamped session-<timestamp>.log file in %LOCALAPPDATA%\appium-wincore-driver\
  • a path ending in \ or /: writes a timestamped file into that folder
  • any other path: writes to exactly that file

docs.title: perfMetrics
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:perfMetrics boolean false

Enables per-session performance counters for the driver's internal calls. Read them with windows: getPerfMetrics and reset them with windows: resetPerfMetrics. See the Performance Metrics guide.

docs.title: app
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:app string Not specified

The application to automate. Accepts one of:

  • a path to an executable, for example C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe
  • a UWP application user model ID, for example Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App
  • Root, to attach to the whole Windows desktop instead of a single application

Environment variables in %NAME% form are expanded in executable paths.

Cannot be combined with appium:appTopLevelWindow. If neither is provided, the session starts without a root window, and a window must be selected later, for example with windows: switchToWindowByTitle.

docs.title: appTopLevelWindow
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:appTopLevelWindow string Not specified

The handle of an already open top-level window to attach to, as a hexadecimal (0x001A0B2C) or decimal string. Numbers are accepted too and converted to a string. Use this instead of appium:app to automate an application that is already running.

docs.title: appArguments
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:appArguments string Not specified

Command line arguments passed to the application launched by appium:app.

docs.title: appWorkingDir
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:appWorkingDir string Not specified

Working directory for the application launched by appium:app. Environment variables in %NAME% form are expanded.

docs.title: ms:waitForAppLaunch
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:ms:waitForAppLaunch number Not specified

How long to wait for the application window to appear after launch. Values up to 120 are read as seconds, larger values as milliseconds.

The same wait applies when the first window to appear is a splash screen: the driver waits for it to give way to the main window. If this capability is not set, the splash screen wait is 5 seconds.

docs.title: shouldCloseApp
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:shouldCloseApp boolean true

Whether to close the application window when the session ends. Has no effect in Root sessions.

docs.title: ms:forcequit
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:ms:forcequit boolean false

When the application is closed at the end of the session (see appium:shouldCloseApp), kill its process instead of closing its window.

docs.title: prerun
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:prerun object Not specified

A PowerShell script to run before the application is started. Provide either {"script": "..."} or {"command": "..."}.

docs.title: postrun
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:postrun object Not specified

A PowerShell script to run after the session ends. Provide either {"script": "..."} or {"command": "..."}.

docs.title: isolatedScriptExecution
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:isolatedScriptExecution boolean false

Runs PowerShell scripts (windows: powerShell, appium:prerun and appium:postrun) without loading the user profile.

docs.title: smoothPointerMove
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:smoothPointerMove string Not specified

Easing curve for mouse pointer moves. Accepts linear, ease, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, or a cubic-bezier(x1,y1,x2,y2) expression. If not set, the pointer jumps directly to its target.

docs.title: delayBeforeClick
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:delayBeforeClick number 0

Duration of the pointer move to an element before clicking it, in milliseconds. Combine with appium:smoothPointerMove for a visible, human-like movement.

docs.title: delayAfterClick
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:delayAfterClick number 50 (100 for menu items)

Time to wait after each click, in milliseconds.

docs.title: Webview
docs.text: See the Hybrid Mode guide for more details about these capabilities.

docs.title: webviewEnabled
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:webviewEnabled boolean false

Enables automation of WebView2, Chrome and Edge content over the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

docs.title: webviewDevtoolsPort
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:webviewDevtoolsPort number Selected automatically

The remote debugging port to connect to. For WebView2 applications launched by the driver, the port is selected and injected automatically.

docs.title: chromedriverExecutablePath
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromedriverExecutablePath string Not specified

Path to a local Chromedriver binary to use instead of downloading one.

docs.title: edgedriverExecutablePath
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:edgedriverExecutablePath string Not specified

Path to a local Microsoft Edge WebDriver (msedgedriver) binary to use instead of downloading one.

docs.title: chromedriverCdnUrl
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromedriverCdnUrl string Not specified

Custom CDN URL to download Chromedriver from.

docs.title: edgedriverCdnUrl
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:edgedriverCdnUrl string Not specified

Custom CDN URL to download Microsoft Edge WebDriver from.

docs.title: ffmpegExecutablePath
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:ffmpegExecutablePath string Not specified

Path to a local FFmpeg binary, used by screen recording.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
The following capabilities are accepted for compatibility with existing Windows test suites, but have no effect:

  • appium:ms:experimental-webdriver
  • appium:deviceName
  • appium:systemPort (the driver does not use a network port to talk to WincoreServer.exe)

docs.title: Element Attributes
docs.text:
The WinCore driver exposes element properties from UI Automation (UIA) and from Microsoft Active Accessibility (MSAA).

The attributes listed in the first part of this page are included in the page source for every element, and can be used in XPath locators. In the page source, all values are strings, booleans are true or false, and an attribute that does not apply to an element is an empty string. The element's tag name is its programmatic control type name, such as Button or Edit.

All of these attributes, and the additional attributes at the end of this page, can also be retrieved with the standard Get Element Attribute endpoint. Attribute names are case-insensitive there.

docs.title: AcceleratorKey
docs.text:
Example: Ctrl+S

The shortcut key combination that invokes the element's action.

docs.title: AccessKey
docs.text:
Example: Alt+F

The access key (mnemonic) that activates the element.

docs.title: AutomationId
docs.text:
Example: num5Button

The identifier assigned to the element by its developer. Used by the accessibility id locator strategy.

docs.title: ClassName
docs.text:
Example: Button

The class name of the element's underlying control. Used by the class name locator strategy.

docs.title: FrameworkId
docs.text:
Example: WPF

The UI framework that the element belongs to, such as Win32, WinForm, WPF or XAML.

docs.title: HasKeyboardFocus
docs.text:
Example: false

Whether the element has keyboard focus.

docs.title: HelpText
docs.text:
Example: Saves the current document

Help text associated with the element, usually its tooltip.

docs.title: IsContentElement
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is part of the content view of the UIA tree.

docs.title: IsControlElement
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is part of the control view of the UIA tree.

docs.title: IsEnabled
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is enabled.

docs.title: IsKeyboardFocusable
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element can receive keyboard focus.

docs.title: IsOffscreen
docs.text:
Example: false

Whether the element is outside of the visible screen area.

docs.title: IsPassword
docs.text:
Example: false

Whether the element contains protected content, such as a password field. On such elements, Value and LegacyValue are always empty in the page source.

docs.title: IsRequiredForForm
docs.text:
Example: false

Whether the element must be filled in on a form.

docs.title: ItemStatus
docs.text:
Example: Busy

A free-form status string reported by the element.

docs.title: ItemType
docs.text:
Example: Document

A free-form description of the type of item the element represents.

docs.title: LocalizedControlType
docs.text:
Example: button

The control type name in the language of the operating system. Used by the tag name locator strategy when given in lowercase.

docs.title: Name
docs.text:
Example: Five

The element's visible label. Used by the name locator strategy.

docs.title: Orientation
docs.text:
Example: 0

The orientation of the element as a number: 0 (none), 1 (horizontal) or 2 (vertical).

docs.title: ProcessId
docs.text:
Example: 4242

The ID of the process that owns the element.

docs.title: RuntimeId
docs.text:
Example: 42.1311890.4.12

The element's UIA runtime identifier, as dot-separated numbers. Used by the id locator strategy.

docs.title: x, y, width, height
docs.text:
Example: x="120" y="210" width="80" height="60"

The element's bounding rectangle in screen coordinates. Omitted when the element has no bounding rectangle.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
Example: Degraded

The element's value, from ValuePattern.Value. See the Standard Accessibility Values guide.

docs.title: LegacyValue
docs.text:
Example: db-01;Running;Degraded

The MSAA value (accValue), from LegacyIAccessible.Value. Often holds the real content of legacy grid cells and rows. See the Standard Accessibility Values guide.

docs.title: LegacyName
docs.text:
Example: Status row 2

The MSAA name, from LegacyIAccessible.Name.

docs.title: LegacyDescription
docs.text:
Example: Server status

The MSAA description, from LegacyIAccessible.Description.

docs.title: LegacyRole
docs.text:
Example: 29

The MSAA role number, from LegacyIAccessible.Role.

docs.title: LegacyState
docs.text:
Example: 1048576

The MSAA state bits, from LegacyIAccessible.State.

docs.title: Additional Attributes
docs.text: The following attributes are not included in the page source, but can be retrieved with the Get Element Attribute endpoint.

docs.title: BoundingRectangle
docs.text:
Example: {"x": 120, "y": 210, "width": 80, "height": 60}

The element's bounding rectangle in screen coordinates, as an object.

docs.title: ClickablePoint
docs.text:
Example: {"x": 160, "y": 240}

A point on the element that can be clicked, as an object. Returns an error if the element has no clickable point.

docs.title: ControlType
docs.text:
Example: Button

The programmatic control type name, which is also the element's tag name. Elements whose control type has no standard name report Custom.

docs.title: Culture
docs.text:
Example: 1033

The locale identifier of the element.

docs.title: ExpandCollapseState
docs.text:
Example: Collapsed

One of Expanded, Collapsed, PartiallyExpanded or LeafNode. For MSAA elements without the UIA ExpandCollapse pattern, it is read from the MSAA state bits. Returns an error if the element reports no expand/collapse state.

docs.title: HeadingLevel
docs.text:
Example: 80051

The UIA heading level identifier of the element.

docs.title: IsDialog
docs.text:
Example: false

Whether the element is a dialog window.

docs.title: Is<Pattern>PatternAvailable
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element supports a given UIA control pattern. Available for the Dock, ExpandCollapse, GridItem, Grid, Invoke, MultipleView, RangeValue, SelectionItem, Selection, Scroll, ScrollItem, Table, TableItem, Text, Toggle, Transform, Value, Window and LegacyIAccessible patterns, for example IsInvokePatternAvailable.

docs.title: LegacyDefaultAction
docs.text:
Example: Press

The MSAA default action, from LegacyIAccessible.DefaultAction.

docs.title: NativeWindowHandle
docs.text:
Example: 1706316

The handle of the element's native window, if it has one.

docs.title: PositionInSet, SizeOfSet
docs.text:
Example: 2, 5

The element's position within its group, and the size of that group, for example for list items.

docs.title: ProviderDescription
docs.text: A description of the UIA provider that serves the element. It names the provider, for example MSAA Proxy for elements bridged from MSAA, which helps to understand why an element behaves the way it does.

docs.title: Pattern-Qualified Aliases
docs.text:
The following names are accepted as aliases:

Name Same as Value.Value Value Value.IsReadOnly Whether the element's value is read-only SelectionItem.IsSelected Whether the element is selected LegacyIAccessible.Value LegacyValue LegacyIAccessible.Name LegacyName LegacyIAccessible.Description LegacyDescription LegacyIAccessible.Role LegacyRole LegacyIAccessible.State LegacyState LegacyIAccessible.DefaultAction LegacyDefaultAction

docs.title: Execute Methods
docs.text:
Invoke all execute methods via executeScript:

await driver.executeScript('windows: <command>', [args]);

Pattern commands that take a single element accept the element reference directly as the first array item:

const btn = await driver.$('~myButton');
await driver.executeScript('windows: invoke', [btn]);

docs.title: windows: click
docs.text:
Simulates a mouse click at a screen coordinate or on a UI element.

Argument Type Required Description elementId string no Click element center; coords become relative x number no Horizontal coordinate y number no Vertical coordinate button string no left (default), middle, right, back, forward modifierKeys string/string[] no Hold keys: shift, ctrl, alt, win durationMs number no Hold time between press and release times number no Repeat count. Default: 1 interClickDelayMs number no Delay between clicks. Default: 100 ms

docs.title: windows: hover
docs.text:
Moves the mouse from a start position to an end position.

Argument Type Required Description startElementId string no Move from element center startX number no Start X coordinate startY number no Start Y coordinate endElementId string no Move to element center endX number no End X coordinate endY number no End Y coordinate modifierKeys string/string[] no Hold keys during move durationMs number no Duration. Default: 500 ms

docs.title: windows: scroll
docs.text:
Mouse wheel scroll. Provide either deltaX or deltaY.

Argument Type Required Description elementId string no Scroll relative to element center x number no Scroll point X y number no Scroll point Y deltaX number no Horizontal ticks (negative = left) deltaY number no Vertical ticks (negative = toward user) modifierKeys string/string[] no Hold keys during scroll

docs.title: windows: clickAndDrag
docs.text:
Press, drag to a target, and release. Provide either startElementId or startX+startY; same for the end point.

Argument Type Required Description startElementId string no Drag start element startX number no Drag start X startY number no Drag start Y endElementId string no Drag end element endX number no Drag end X endY number no Drag end Y button string no Mouse button. Default: left modifierKeys string/string[] no Hold keys during drag durationMs number no Drag duration. Default: 500 ms

docs.title: windows: keys
docs.text:
Sends a sequence of keyboard actions.

Argument Type Required Description actions KeyAction or KeyAction[] yes Sequence of key actions forceUnicode boolean no Send as Unicode; disables modifier combos

Each KeyAction must contain exactly one of:

Property Type Description pause number Pause in milliseconds text string Unicode text to type virtualKeyCode number Windows virtual-key code (e.g. 0x0D = Enter)

When using virtualKeyCode, the optional down boolean presses the key (true), releases it (false), or taps it (omit down). Always release any key that was explicitly pressed down.

See the full list of virtual-key codes at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/inputdev/virtual-key-codes.

// Ctrl+A — select all
await driver.executeScript('windows: keys', [{
  actions: [
    { virtualKeyCode: 0x11, down: true },   // Ctrl down
    { virtualKeyCode: 0x41, down: true },   // A down
    { virtualKeyCode: 0x41, down: false },  // A up
    { virtualKeyCode: 0x11, down: false },  // Ctrl up
  ],
}]);

docs.title: UI Pattern Commands
docs.text:
The following commands each take a single element reference as their only argument:

Command UIA Pattern Description windows: invoke InvokePattern Activate the element windows: expand ExpandCollapsePattern Expand the element windows: collapse ExpandCollapsePattern Collapse the element windows: toggle TogglePattern Toggle element state windows: select SelectionItemPattern Select in a list/combo windows: addToSelection SelectionItemPattern Add to selection windows: removeFromSelection SelectionItemPattern Remove from selection windows: scrollIntoView ScrollItemPattern Scroll into view windows: setFocus — Set keyboard focus

windows: select, windows: expand and windows: collapse check that they took effect. If the element still reports the old state, they fail with invalid element state instead of returning success.

How the check works:

  • Real UIA patterns are trusted. On elements with their own UIA provider (WPF, UWP, UIA's built-in Win32 proxies), the command calls the pattern and returns success if it doesn't throw.
  • MSAA-backed elements are verified. DevExpress, the .NET Framework DataGridView, and VB6 / Delphi / MFC controls reach UIA through the MSAA Proxy, whose calls report success whether or not anything happened. After acting, the command checks the state once (briefly polling). An element that disappears in the meantime (a re-created row, a closed popup) counts as done.
  • select: SelectionItemPattern, then on MSAA elements LegacyIAccessible.Select. The fallback makes DataGridView cells selectable.
  • expand / collapse: read the current state first and do nothing when the element is already there. MSAA elements without ExpandCollapsePattern (group rows, legacy tree grids) use their default action. An MSAA element that reports no state is acted on without verification. One with no state and no default action reports "not supported", so the client's ALT+Down fallback runs.
  • ComboBoxes keep the ALT+Down fallback, also after invalid element state. The state is checked again afterwards: if ALT+Down changed nothing, the command fails with the original error, or with invalid element state when the pattern call had reported success.

Behaviour changes from earlier versions:

  • select / expand / collapse on MSAA elements fail with invalid element state where they used to return success without effect.
  • expand on an already expanded MSAA group no longer collapses it.
  • select without SelectionItemPattern on a non-MSAA element fails with "does not support SelectionItemPattern", as before. collapse without ExpandCollapsePattern on a non-MSAA element fails the same way and never runs the element's default action.
  • getAttribute('ExpandCollapseState') errors on an element that reports no state. It used to return LeafNode.
  • windows: invoke calls the real InvokePattern. On elements that have both Invoke and SelectionItem it now invokes instead of selecting.

docs.title: windows: selectFromCombobox
docs.text:
Opens a combo box (or any list / tree container), finds the entry whose text is exactly value, and selects it.

Param Type Required Description elementId string yes The combo box or container element value string yes Exact text (Name) of the entry to select 
await driver.executeScript('windows: selectFromCombobox', [
  {elementId: await combo.elementId, value: 'Finance'},
]);
// or, like windows: setValue, as two arguments:
await driver.executeScript('windows: selectFromCombobox', [combo, 'Finance']);

Steps:

  1. Expands the container unless it is already open. A container without ExpandCollapsePattern (a list box, a tree) is searched as it is.
  2. Asks the container for the entry through UI Automation's ItemContainerPattern. This reaches entries a virtualized list (WPF) has not created yet; the entry is realized (VirtualizedItemPattern) so it can be selected. A container from a server plugin is asked through its tree provider's FindItemInContainer instead, when the plugin implements it.
  3. Otherwise looks for a descendant whose Name equals value. List, data, tree and menu items win over other elements with the same text, such as the combo's selection box. WinForms, Win32 and MSAA lists expose every entry once open.
  4. Selects the entry as windows: select does, then closes the popup if it is still open.

Name matching is exact (case-sensitive, no partial match). If no entry matches, the popup is closed and the command fails with no such element. The popup's entries must be descendants of the container element; a dropdown that opens as a separate top-level window is not searched.

docs.title: windows: setValue
docs.text: Sets the element value via ValuePattern. Arg 0: element. Arg 1: value string.

docs.title: windows: getValue
docs.text: Returns the element's current value string. Arg 0: element.

docs.title: windows: selectedItem
docs.text: Returns the selected element from a selection container. Arg 0: container element.

docs.title: windows: allSelectedItems
docs.text: Returns all selected elements as an array. Arg 0: container element.

docs.title: windows: isMultiple
docs.text: Returns true if the container supports multi-select. Arg 0: container element.

docs.title: windows: maximize / minimize / restore / close
docs.text: Window state control via WindowPattern. Arg 0: window element.

docs.title: windows: launchApp
docs.text: Re-launches the app from the appium:app capability. No arguments.

docs.title: windows: closeApp
docs.text: Closes the current root application window. No arguments.

docs.title: windows: getWindows
docs.text:
Returns all visible top-level windows including untitled windows that the standard WebDriver getWindowHandles() omits.

Each entry in the returned array contains:

Field Type Description handle string Hex window handle (e.g. 0x000a1234) — pass directly to driver.switchToWindow() title string Window title. Empty string "" for untitled windows className string Win32 window class name (e.g. Notepad, #32770)

Difference from getWindowHandles(): The standard getWindowHandles() only returns windows with a non-empty title. windows: getWindows returns all visible windows and provides richer metadata, making it possible to locate and switch to untitled popups and dialogs by their class name or handle.

const windows = await driver.executeScript('windows: getWindows', []);
// [
//   { handle: '0x000a1234', title: 'My App', className: 'Notepad' },
//   { handle: '0x000b5678', title: '',        className: '#32770' },
// ]

// Switch to an untitled dialog by class name
const popup = windows.find(w => w.className === '#32770' && w.title === '');
await driver.switchToWindow(popup.handle);

docs.title: windows: switchToWindowByTitle
docs.text:
Switches the session to a window matched by title. Uses Win32 EnumWindows so it always searches all visible top-level windows regardless of where the session is currently rooted.

Argument Type Required Description title string Yes Title string to match against exact boolean No true for exact case-insensitive match. Default: false (substring match)

Throws NoSuchWindowError if no window matches after the implicit timeout.

// Partial match — finds "Untitled - Notepad", "My Doc - Notepad", etc.
await driver.executeScript('windows: switchToWindowByTitle', [{ title: 'Notepad' }]);

// Exact match
await driver.executeScript('windows: switchToWindowByTitle', [{ title: 'Untitled - Notepad', exact: true }]);

docs.title: Switching back to the desktop root
docs.text:
Pass the sentinel string 'root' to driver.switchToWindow() to reset the session root back to the Windows desktop element. Useful after switching to a specific app window or a titleless system pane (e.g. system tray overflow).

// Switch to some app window
await driver.switchToWindow(someHandle);

// ... do work ...

// Return to full desktop root
await driver.switchToWindow('root');

docs.title: windows: getWindowElement
docs.text: Returns the automation element ID of the current root window. No arguments.

docs.title: windows: getDeviceTime
docs.text:
Returns the Windows system time as a string.

Argument Type Description format string Optional. The format of the returned string. Defaults to yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:sszzz (ISO 8601). By default it is a .NET custom date and time format string, e.g. yyyy-MM-dd (not moment.js YYYY-MM-DD). formatSyntax string Optional. dotnet (default) or moment. With moment, format is in moment.js notation, as in the other Appium drivers, e.g. YYYY-MM-DD. Supported tokens: YYYY YY MMMM MMM MM M DD D dddd ddd HH H hh h mm m ss s SSS SS S A Z ZZ (ZZ is written with a colon, like Z); text in [brackets] and other characters are kept as is.

docs.title: windows: getMonitors
docs.text:
Returns an array of monitor descriptors. No arguments.

Property Type Description index number Zero-based monitor index deviceName string Device name, e.g. \\.\DISPLAY1 primary boolean true for the primary display bounds object { x, y, width, height } in virtual screen coords workingArea object Usable area excluding taskbars 
const monitors = await driver.executeScript('windows: getMonitors', [{}]);
const secondary = monitors.find(m => !m.primary);
if (secondary) {
  await driver.setWindowRect(
    secondary.bounds.x, secondary.bounds.y, null, null
  );
}

docs.title: windows: getDpiScale
docs.text: Returns the primary display's DPI scaling factor as a number, e.g. 1.5 for 150% scaling. No arguments.

docs.title: windows: getNativeChildren
docs.text:
Walks the raw MSAA (IAccessible) tree of an element, for legacy controls that expose no UIA children (custom-drawn Win32 controls, ActiveX grids).

Argument Type Required Description elementId string yes The element whose MSAA children are walked

Returns { supported: true, node }, where each node has name, role, value, description, state, defaultAction, rect, childCount, truncated and children, or { supported: false, reason } when the element has no IAccessible implementation. If it is unsupported or the root has no children, fall back to image- or coordinate-based interaction.

docs.title: windows: getPerfMetrics
docs.text: Returns the session's performance counters as { enabled, metrics: { totalCalls, totalMs, byLabel: { <label>: { count, totalMs } } } }. Counters are only collected when the session was created with appium:perfMetrics: true; otherwise enabled is false and metrics is empty. No arguments. See the Performance Metrics guide.

docs.title: windows: resetPerfMetrics
docs.text: Zeroes the session's performance counters, so the counts that follow belong to the next operation alone. No arguments.

docs.title: windows: getClipboard
docs.text:
Returns base64-encoded clipboard content.

Argument Type Required Description contentType 'plaintext' / 'image' no Default: 'plaintext'

docs.title: windows: setClipboard
docs.text: Argument Type Required Description b64Content string yes Base64-encoded content contentType 'plaintext' / 'image' no Default: 'plaintext'

docs.text:
Requires the modify_fs insecure feature.

Argument Type Required Description path string yes Absolute path to the file

docs.title: windows: deleteFolder
docs.text:
Requires the modify_fs insecure feature.

Argument Type Required Description path string yes Absolute path to the folder recursive boolean no Delete recursively. Default: true

docs.title: Screen Recording
docs.text: Records the whole desktop with ffmpeg (gdigrab input, H.264 in an mp4 file). The driver looks for ffmpeg in appium:ffmpegExecutablePath first, then at ffmpeg fmpeg.exe in the driver's folder. If neither exists, it downloads the latest build from GitHub into that folder on first use, which needs network access. Any build you supply must include gdigrab.

docs.title: windows: startRecordingScreen
docs.text:
Begins recording the screen. All arguments are optional.

Argument Type Default Description outputPath string temp file Where to write the video, on the machine running Appium. Must end in .mp4 timeLimit number 600 Maximum duration in seconds. ffmpeg stops by itself at this limit videoFps number 15 Frames per second preset string veryfast libx264 encoder preset, e.g. ultrafast videoFilter string none ffmpeg video filter, passed to -filter:v audioInput string none DirectShow audio device name to record from forceRestart boolean true When a recording is running: true discards it and starts a new one, false keeps it and does nothing captureCursor boolean false See the warning below captureClicks boolean false See the warning below

Starting a recording deletes the file of the previous one, even if it was already stopped. Copy the file first if you set outputPath and want to keep it.

Warning

Do not set captureCursor or captureClicks to true. ffmpeg rejects the flags they add for gdigrab input, so the command fails with "The expected screen record file does not exist". The mouse pointer is always recorded, whatever captureCursor says, and clicks cannot be highlighted.

Warning

videoFilter replaces the driver's built-in filter, which pads the video to even dimensions. On a desktop with an odd width or height, include your own padding or scaling, or the recording fails.

docs.title: windows: stopRecordingScreen
docs.text:
Stops recording. Without remotePath, it returns the video as a base64-encoded string. With remotePath, it uploads the video and returns an empty string. It also returns an empty string when no recording was started.

All arguments are optional.

Argument Type Default Description remotePath string none HTTP(S) URL to upload the video to user string none Basic auth user name. Needs pass too pass string none Basic auth password. Needs user too method string PUT HTTP method of the upload headers object none Extra HTTP headers fileFieldName string file Multipart form field holding the video. An empty string sends the video as the raw request body formFields object or array none Extra multipart form fields, as an object or an array of [name, value] pairs

The video file stays on disk after stopping. Stop any running recording before ending the session, because the driver does not stop it for you; it runs until timeLimit.

await driver.executeScript('windows: startRecordingScreen', [{
  videoFps: 30,
  timeLimit: 120,
}]);
// ... run your test ...
const video = await driver.executeScript(
  'windows: stopRecordingScreen', [{}]
);
// video is a base64-encoded mp4

// Or upload it instead
await driver.executeScript('windows: stopRecordingScreen', [{
  remotePath: 'https://example.com/recordings/run-42.mp4',
  user: 'ci',
  pass: 'secret',
}]);

docs.title: powerShell
docs.text:
Executes a PowerShell script and returns its trimmed stdout. Anything written to stderr fails the command with that text.

The script name is powerShell (there is no windows: prefix). The argument is the script as a string, or an object with a script (or command) property.

Each call starts a new powershell.exe process, so variables, functions and the current location do not carry over from one call to the next. Put everything a step needs into one script. The process starts in appium:appWorkingDir when that capability is set. With appium:isolatedScriptExecution set to true, the process is started without loading the user profile.

const output = await driver.executeScript('powerShell', [
  'Get-Process notepad -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue',
]);

// Object form
const year = await driver.executeScript('powerShell', [
  { script: 'Get-Date -Format yyyy' },
]);

docs.title: windows: cacheRequest
docs.text:
Activates a UIA cache request, for example to expose RawView elements in the element tree. All arguments are optional, but at least one must be set.

Argument Type Required Description treeFilter string no UIA condition, e.g. RawView treeScope string no Element, Children, or Subtree automationElementMode string no None or Full. Default: Full 
await driver.executeScript('windows: cacheRequest', [{ treeFilter: 'RawView' }]);

docs.title: Insecure Features
docs.text:
Some insecure driver features are disabled by default. They can be enabled upon launching Appium as follows:

appium --allow-insecure wincore:<feature-name>

or

appium --relaxed-security

For other insecure feature names recognized by the Appium server, see their Appium docs reference page.

docs.title: modify_fs
docs.text: Allows changing the file system of the machine running Appium. Required by windows: deleteFile, windows: deleteFolder, and the standard Push File and Pull File commands.

docs.title: Locator Strategies
docs.text:
The WinCore driver supports several location strategies. The list below describes each strategy along with usage recommendations.

Each strategy lists two speed grades, from A+ (fastest) to D (slowest):

  • Absolute: a lookup from the driver (driver.findElement / driver.findElements), which searches the whole subtree of the session window. In Root sessions, this walks across all open desktop windows.
  • Relative: a lookup from an element (element.findElement / element.findElements), which only searches that element's subtree.

All strategies except XPath run as a native UI Automation (UIA) condition search, which is evaluated inside UIA's own tree traversal and stops at the first match for a single-element lookup. See Absolute vs. Relative Lookup for how to keep slower lookups fast.

docs.title: Id
docs.text:
Name Absolute Relative Example id A+ A+ 42.1311890.4.12

This strategy matches the element's RuntimeId, as dot-separated numbers. Runtime IDs are assigned by UIA and change between application runs.

When to Use

Use this strategy to find an element again after reading its RuntimeId, for example from the page source.

docs.title: Accessibility Id
docs.text:
Name Absolute Relative Example accessibility id A+ A+ SubmitButton

This strategy matches the element's AutomationId exactly. The value is stored directly on the element, without any locale formatting.

When to Use

Use this strategy whenever the element has an AutomationId. It is the fastest and most stable strategy.

docs.title: Name
docs.text:
Name Absolute Relative Example name B A OK

This strategy matches the element's visible label, Name, exactly. Computing the name of complex or MSAA-bridged controls is slightly more expensive than reading an AutomationId.

When to Use

Use this strategy for elements without an AutomationId, if their label is stable. Labels are usually localized, so they change with the language of the application.

docs.title: Class Name
docs.text:
Name Absolute Relative Example class name A A TextBlock

This strategy matches the element's ClassName exactly. Finding many elements costs more as the number of matches grows.

When to Use

Use this strategy for elements that can be identified by the class of their underlying control.

docs.title: Tag Name
docs.text:
Name Absolute Relative Example tag name (PascalCase) A A Button tag name (lowercase) B A button

This strategy matches the element's control type:

  • A PascalCase name, such as Button or CheckBox, matches the programmatic ControlType. It is compared as a number, so it is fast and works the same on any Windows display language.
  • A lowercase name, such as button, matches the LocalizedControlType, which is compared as text and depends on the Windows display language.

When to Use

Use the PascalCase form to find elements by their type. Prefer it over the lowercase form.

docs.title: CSS Selector
docs.text:
Name Absolute Relative Example css selector A A+ Button[name="OK"]

This strategy converts a CSS selector to a Windows UIAutomation condition. The conversion takes less than a millisecond, and the condition then runs the same native search.

The tag matches the programmatic control type (Button), #value matches the AutomationId and .value matches the ClassName. Supported attributes are name, automation-id (aliases id and accessibility-id), class-name (alias class), control-type, localized-control-type, help-text, framework-id, item-status and item-type. Boolean attributes such as enabled are not supported.

When to Use

Use this strategy to combine several conditions in a compact form.

docs.title: Windows UIAutomation
docs.text:
Name Absolute Relative Example -windows uiautomation A A+ new PropertyCondition(AutomationElement.NameProperty, 'OK')

This strategy accepts a UIA condition, written as in C# or PowerShell with System.Windows.Automation. PropertyCondition, AndCondition, OrCondition and NotCondition are supported. The expression is parsed, not executed.

// exact match
await driver.findElement('-windows uiautomation', "new PropertyCondition(AutomationElement.NameProperty, 'OK')")

// logical AND
await driver.findElement('-windows uiautomation', "new AndCondition(new PropertyCondition(AutomationElement.ControlTypeProperty, ControlType.Button), new PropertyCondition(AutomationElement.NameProperty, 'OK'))")

Narrowing a condition by ControlType together with AutomationId or Name lets UIA skip elements of other types early.

Warning

PropertyConditionFlags such as MatchSubstring and IgnoreCase are not supported. Use XPath contains() for substring matching.

When to Use

Use this strategy for conditions that combine several properties, when no single property identifies the element.

docs.title: XPath
docs.text:
Name Absolute Relative Example xpath D B–C //Button[@Name="OK"]

This strategy relies on the XML tree generated by the driver's page source API. XPath version 2.0 is supported (through XPath2.Net), over all element attributes of the page source. The expression must return elements: an expression returning any other value, such as count(//Button), is an invalid selector. Matching elements are always returned in document order.

Before the expression runs, every element in the searched subtree is read into an XML document, even for a single-element lookup. The cost grows with the size of the subtree: about 1.5 ms per element on WPF, and 3 to 5 ms per element on WinForms and MSAA controls. A lookup in a window of 3,000 elements can take 4.5 to 6 seconds.

Tag names in XPath are the programmatic control type names, such as Button, Edit or DataGrid. They are case-sensitive (//Button matches, //button does not) and the same on any Windows display language. Elements whose control type has no standard name are tagged Custom. When unsure of the tag, match on an attribute instead: //*[@Name="OK"].

Use string functions to match elements by part of an attribute, by a regular expression, or regardless of case:

await driver.$('//*[contains(@Name, "Execute")]')
await driver.$('//Button[starts-with(@Name, "OK")]')
await driver.$('//Button[ends-with(@AutomationId, "Button")]')
await driver.$('//Button[matches(@Name, "^Save( As)?$")]')
await driver.$('//Button[lower-case(@Name) = "ok"]')
await driver.$('//Button[@Name = ("Yes", "OK")]')

Stricter types than XPath 1.0

All attribute values in the page source are strings, and XPath 2.0 does not silently convert them like XPath 1.0 did. Some expressions that worked with XPath 1.0 are now invalid selectors:

  • Comparing an attribute to a number fails as soon as one element has a non-numeric value, for example //Button[@Name = 7] when another button is named Plus. Quote the value instead: //Button[@Name = "7"].
  • Numeric comparisons on attributes that are often empty fail for the same reason, for example //*[@Value > 5]. Convert the value explicitly: //*[number(@Value) > 5].
  • String functions accept a single value, so //Window[contains(.//Text/@Name, "Total")] fails when the window has several Text elements. Move the condition onto the element instead: //Window[.//Text[contains(@Name, "Total")]].

Comparing a boolean attribute to true() now compares its value: //Button[@IsEnabled = true()] only matches enabled buttons, while XPath 1.0 matched every button that had the attribute. Comparing to a string (@IsEnabled = "true") works the same in both versions.

When to Use

Use this strategy when no other strategy is applicable: for substring matching, positional predicates, matching on standard accessibility values, or elements that can only be identified from their parent, sibling or descendant elements. On large windows, use it as a relative lookup.

docs.title: Absolute vs. Relative Lookup
docs.text:
An absolute lookup searches the whole session window. A relative lookup starts from an element that was already found, and searches only that element's subtree.

When XPath is needed on a large window, find the container with a fast strategy first, then run a relative XPath lookup inside it:

// Slow (~4.5 s on a 3,000-element window): reads the whole window into XML
const rowSlow = await driver.$('//DataItem[starts-with(@LegacyValue, "db-01;")]');

// Fast (~50-100 ms): finds the grid by AutomationId, then reads only the grid into XML
const grid = await driver.$('~ServersGrid');
const rowFast = await grid.$('.//DataItem[starts-with(@LegacyValue, "db-01;")]');
